records.label: Two families with biallelic CSF3 variants
records.segregation: each family segregating a different biallelic inactivating variant with SCN
quotes: Here, we describe three patients from two families each segregating a different biallelic inactivating variant in CSF3 with SCN.
Our results suggest that CSF3 deficiency in humans causes a novel autosomal recessive form of SCN.

records.label: Patient(s) with homozygous CSF3 loss-of-function variant

variants.as_reported: homozygous pathogenic loss-of-function variant in CSF3

quotes: We present the first confirmatory report of a previously proposed SCN due to a homozygous pathogenic loss-of-function variant in CSF3.

notes.statement: Almannai et al. (2026) presented what they described as the first confirmatory report of severe congenital neutropenia due to a homozygous pathogenic loss-of-function variant in CSF3, supporting this gene-disease relationship in humans.
quotes: We present the first confirmatory report of a previously proposed SCN due to a homozygous pathogenic loss-of-function variant in CSF3.
Our report supports this new gene-disease relationship in humans.

notes.statement: Khouj et al. (2023) demonstrated complete deficiency of CSF3 resulting from nonsense-mediated decay by RT-PCR of RNA derived from patient skin fibroblasts.
quotes: Complete deficiency of CSF3 as a result of nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) could be demonstrated on RT-PCR using skin fibroblasts-derived RNA.

notes.statement: Khouj et al. (2023) noted that the phenotype in their patients with CSF3 deficiency mirrored that documented in mouse and zebrafish models of CSF3 deficiency.
quotes: The phenotype observed in this cohort mirrors that documented in mouse and zebrafish models of CSF3 deficiency.

notes.statement: Lieschke et al. (1994) generated mice lacking G-CSF by targeted disruption in embryonic stem cells. The G-CSF-null mice were viable, fertile, and superficially healthy but had chronic neutropenia, with peripheral blood neutrophil levels 20 to 30% of wildtype. Heterozygous mice had intermediate neutrophil levels, which suggested a gene-dosage effect.
quotes: G-CSF-deficient mice (genotype G-CSF-/-) are viable, fertile, and superficially healthy, but have a chronic neutropenia.

Peripheral blood neutrophil levels were 20% to 30% of wild-type mice (genotype G-CSF+/+) and mice heterozygous for the null mutation had intermediate neutrophil levels, suggesting a gene-dosage effect.

notes.statement: Lieschke et al. (1994) found that in G-CSF-null mice, marrow granulopoietic precursor cells were reduced by 50%, and granulocyte, macrophage, and blast progenitor cells were reduced. Mature neutrophils were still present in blood and marrow, which indicated that other factors can support neutrophil production in vivo.
quotes: In the marrow of G-CSF-/- mice, granulopoietic precursor cells were reduced by 50% and there were reduced levels of granulocyte, macrophage, and blast progenitor cells.
Despite G-CSF deficiency, mature neutrophils were still present in the blood and marrow, indicating that other factors can support neutrophil production in vivo.

notes.statement: Lieschke et al. (1994) found that giving G-CSF reversed the granulopoietic defect of G-CSF-null mice. One day of treatment brought circulating neutrophils to normal levels, and after 4 days the null marrow could not be told apart from wildtype marrow by morphology. Fewer neutrophils were available for rapid mobilization by a single dose of G-CSF.
quotes: G-CSF administration reversed the granulopoietic defect of G-CSF-/- mice. One day of G-CSF administration to G-CSF-/- mice elevated circulating neutrophil levels to normal, and after 4 days of G-CSF administration, G-CSF+/+ and G-CSF-/- marrows were morphologically indistinguishable.
G-CSF-/- mice had reduced numbers of neutrophils available for rapid mobilization into the circulation by a single dose of G-CSF.

notes.statement: Lieschke et al. (1994) found that G-CSF-null mice were markedly impaired in controlling Listeria monocytogenes infection. They had smaller neutrophil increases and delayed monocyte increases in the blood, and less infection-driven granulopoiesis. The authors concluded that G-CSF is indispensable for maintaining normal steady-state neutrophil production and is involved in emergency granulopoiesis.
quotes: G-CSF-/- mice had a markedly impaired ability to control infection with Listeria monocytogenes, with diminished neutrophil and delayed monocyte increases in the blood and reduced infection-driven granulopoiesis.
these observations indicate that G-CSF is indispensible for maintaining the normal quantitative balance of neutrophil production during "steady-state" granulopoiesis in vivo
